name: Reuben Sawyer
life: “I still remember the smell of a new envelope containing an old promise.” People around the corner outside Coastal Barber know Reuben by a small Thursday habit. Reuben usually checks the board before the regulars give a more colorful account of the news.
voice: I want one share for my grandson so somebody younger will keep asking how the rent is set.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for an old plum windbreaker and a folded shopping list secured by a miniature clip. Reuben has a small notch in the left eyebrow, with a neat white crop. Reuben turns fully toward the person speaking during a conversation.
personality: Reuben uses precise names for tools and very approximate names for feelings. People who know Reuben well listen to what gets repaired after a difficult conversation.
agenda: To buy a share the grandson can responsibly vote.
family: Gus Lark is Reuben’s cousin. Reuben chooses whether to use it. Gus saves a place. The invitation means something because declining it has never ended the friendship between their households. Asked about *The porch light*, Gus says, “I sold the owner two bulbs every winter. He always wrote my name in a little book beside the price.”
connections: Rain Salcedo. A silent shareholder discusses what a child would gain from one small voting share.

reactions.situation: An unexpected dividend arrives in the wrong envelope
reactions.response: Reuben checks the payee's name with the teller before opening the envelope.

reactions.situation: A family supper turns into an argument about old debt
reactions.response: Reuben asks each person to say what they believe is actually owed before anybody proposes a payment.
